title: VerificationLedger
description: Plugin-native verification output. Separates what the agent team produced into supported claims, challenged claims, unresolved tensions, and human-required checks. This is the core anti-sycophancy object: Argus does not promote a scaffold until the verification state is visible.

overall_status.description: verified = no critical blockers; mixed = usable with caveats; needs_revision = agent team should revise before boss/user signoff; blocked = requires human/external evidence first.

confidence.description: Confidence in the verification result, not in the business decision.

supported_claims.description: Positive validation: claims that are supported by worker evidence, code citations, source references, or cross-agent agreement.

source.description: worker_id, file path, PR ref, or external source label.

challenged_claims.description: Negative validation: claims that are unsupported, too generic, contradicted, risky, or likely to produce false confidence.

unresolved_tensions.description: Real disagreements that should remain visible to the user instead of being averaged away.

human_required_checks.description: Things AI cannot verify from the available repo/session context. These are immediate user/external checks, not long-term outcome grading.

claim_tests.description: Positive/negative tests the verifier applied. Useful for debugging why a claim was supported or challenged.

routing_decision.description: Next routing selected by /argus:verify. sail respects this unless the user explicitly overrides.

user_choice.description: Recorded AskUserQuestion result when the verifier had to ask the user how to handle challenged or blocked claims.
